These rules apply to everyone and are enforced automatically by the database: nobody, not even the administrators, can apply them differently without leaving a trace. The numbers below are read live from the configuration.
You need to sign in to contribute. Credibility goes from 0 to {cred_max} and everyone starts with {cred_start}.
Contribution approved by the majority: +{gain_approved}. Just posting earns no points.
Contribution refuted by the majority: −{loss_refuted}. If the refutation is reversed, the points come back.
Whoever refutes must write a justification. The justification can also be approved or refuted and is worth ±{gain_just} to its author.
Credibility is always recalculated from the current result of the votes, so anyone can check the math.
Simple majority wins; for now, a single vote is enough.
The result always follows the current majority. In a tie (including 0 to 0), the contribution stays up, but it only earns points when there are more approvals than refutations.
A refutation only counts while its justification has not been refuted by the majority (replies and counter-replies follow the same rule).
Nobody votes on what they wrote.
To vote you need credibility {vote_min_cred} or more and an account at least {vote_min_days} days old.
Zero credibility: can no longer contribute.
Anyone can report another person for harassment. The system cross-checks the data from the last {perse_window_days} days and confirms harassment if all three conditions are true at the same time:
Focus on one person: the accused refuted at least {perse_min_refutes} of the reporter's contributions.
Disproportion: more than half of all the accused's refutations in that period were against the reporter.
Unfair refutations: most of those refutations were reversed by the community.
If confirmed: the accused's account is banned and all their refutations against the reporter are annulled (the lost credibility comes back).
If not confirmed: the report is archived and the reporter sees which numbers fell short.
Anyone with {report_strikes} archived reports in a row cannot file reports for {report_block_days} days.
A separate track, without credibility: the request is made through GitHub and approved automatically.
Requirements: a GitHub account at least 6 months old and at least 30 contributions in the last 90 days (they can be on the same day).
And at least 1 merged pull request in someone else's project.
Anyone who doesn't qualify sees exactly what was missing and can ask again later.
Every profile has a public history with each gain and loss and the reason.
The result of every report is public, with the numbers used (the text and the reporter stay private).
The code of the site and of the rules is open on GitHub.

The largest nation in the world, covering almost the entire Great Continent. Diverse and decentralized, with local kings and governors under the authority of Ba Sing Se.
At war with the Fire Nation for a hundred years; it lost territory in the west to the Fire Nation colonies.
Shaken by the fall of the Earth Queen; Kuvira reunifies it by force as the Earth Empire, until she is stopped by Korra.
Volcanic archipelago west of the Great Continent, ruled by the Fire Lord from the Capital.
Industrial and military power waging the Hundred Year War since Sozin's attack on the Air Nomads.
A nation at peace, ruled by Fire Lord Izumi, Zuko's daughter.
Northern polar territory, home of the largest of the Water Tribes.
Southern polar territory, home of the Southern Water Tribe.
A strip in the northwest of the Great Continent colonized by the Fire Nation during the war.
Mixed towns of Fire and Earth people, some more than a century old.
The former colonies form the United Republic of Nations, founded by Aang and Zuko after the Harmony Restoration Movement.
Name given to the devastated world outside the havens, battered by storms after the Cataclysm.
A vast desert in the heart of the Earth Kingdom, crossed by sandbenders on sand sailers.
Appa is captured here by sandbenders.
A living swamp in the southwest of the Earth Kingdom, connected by the roots of a single giant tree. Home to an isolated tribe of waterbenders.
Team Avatar gets lost here and has visions of loved ones.
Toph Beifong lives in the swamp as a hermit and helps Korra recover.
Sea between the Fire Nation and the Great Continent.
Bay where Republic City was built; named after Princess Yue.
Lake crossed by the ferries that carry refugees to Ba Sing Se.
Hidden port in the center of the Earth Kingdom, from which the refugee ferries leave for Ba Sing Se.
Large bay on the east coast of the Great Continent. Identification on the map is estimated.
Meeting point of the Southern Water Tribe fleet led by Hakoda.
One of the four Air Nomad temples, in the Patola Mountain Range, in the Southern Archipelago.
Home of Aang and Monk Gyatso. Abandoned since Sozin's attack a hundred years earlier; Aang returns here and learns the fate of his people.
Kept by the Air Acolytes and visited by Tenzin's family.
Air Nomad temple at the far west end of the Taihua Mountains, in the north of the Great Continent.
Occupied by refugees led by the Mechanist, who filled it with steam-powered contraptions.
Seat of the new Air Nation: Tenzin trains the new airbenders here, until the Red Lotus attack.
A temple built upside down on a cliff face, in a mountain range north of the Fire islands.
Refuge of Team Avatar after the Day of Black Sun; this is where Zuko joins the group.
Ancient temple of the Air Nomad nuns, in a mountain range southeast of the Earth Kingdom.
Aang trains with Guru Pathik to master the Avatar State by opening his chakras.
Island in Yue Bay, facing Republic City.
Home of Tenzin, his family and the Air Acolytes; where Korra learns airbending.
A capital built inside the crater of an extinct volcano, seat of the Royal Palace.
Target of the invasion on the Day of Black Sun; stage of the final Agni Kai between Zuko and Azula.
Seat of Fire Lord Izumi's government.
Summer resort island of the Fire nobility, with beaches and the royal family's beach house.
Team Avatar hides here and watches the play by the Ember Island Players.
Volcanic island in the east of the Fire Nation, home of Avatar Roku's Fire Temple.
Aang speaks with Avatar Roku on the winter solstice; the temple is destroyed by the eruption.
Avatar Roku's home island, in the east of the Fire Nation.
Devastated by an eruption about 70 years ago; Roku died trying to contain it.
Maximum-security prison on an island in the middle of a boiling lake.
Sokka and Zuko break into the prison to rescue Hakoda and Suki.
Ancient city, in the northern islands of the Fire Nation, of the civilization that learned firebending from the dragons.
Zuko and Aang meet the dragons Ran and Shaw and rediscover the true meaning of fire.
Port city with an enormous fire-breathing fountain statue.
Toph and Sokka run scams here until they end up on wanted posters.
Katara confronts Yon Rha, the man responsible for her mother's death.
City of ice and canals, capital of the Northern Water Tribe.
Withstands Admiral Zhao's siege; Princess Yue becomes the Moon Spirit.
Ruled by Unalaq and later by Desna and Eska.
Warm sacred pond where Tui and La, the Moon and Ocean spirits, swim as koi fish.
Passage between the physical world and the Spirit World at the North Pole.
Opened by Korra at the end of Book 2.
Katara and Sokka's small village, where Aang is found in an iceberg.
It grew into a port city; home of Korra and stage of the Water Tribe Civil War.
Passage to the Spirit World at the South Pole, surrounded by the Spirit Wilds.
Reopened by Korra during Harmonic Convergence.
Capital of the Earth Kingdom, surrounded by concentric walls.
Secretly controlled by the Dai Li; falls to Azula at the end of Book 2 and is liberated by the Order of the White Lotus.
Earth Queen Hou-Ting is killed by Zaheer; the city later passes to Kuvira's Earth Empire.

A haven in the northeast of the Great Continent, built where the old Earth Kingdom capital stood; its name preserves its ties to the Old World. It values old traditions and customs. Also called "New Ba".
Lake inside the walls of Ba Sing Se.
Hides the Dai Li's secret base, where Appa was held prisoner.
A great city built on a mountain of the Kolau Mountain Range, in the southwest of the Earth Kingdom; famous for its delivery chutes.
Ruled by the eccentric King Bumi; occupied by the Fire Nation and renamed New Ozai, until it is freed during the eclipse.
Underground labyrinth created by Oma and Shu, the first earthbenders, giving access to Omashu.
City in the south of the Earth Kingdom, home of the wealthy Beifong family.
Toph's hometown, where she secretly fought in the Earth Rumble tournament.
Island created by Avatar Kyoshi when she separated her homeland from the mainland; home of the Kyoshi Warriors.
Team Avatar meets Suki and the Kyoshi Warriors.
Aang is put on trial for Kyoshi's alleged crime against Chin the Conqueror.
Village at the edge of the forest, in the south of the former colonies (later the United Republic), haunted by the spirit Hei Bai.
Aang calms Hei Bai and makes his first journey to the Spirit World.
Village in a valley at the foot of a volcano, in the northeast of the former colonies (later the United Republic); home of the fortuneteller Aunt Wu.
Aang and Katara save the village from an eruption.
The largest canyon in the world.
Aang guides two rival tribes across the canyon.
Run-down oasis on the edge of the Si Wong Desert.
Team Avatar meets Professor Zei, who is searching for the lost library.
Library of the spirit of knowledge, hidden in the desert sands.
Sokka discovers the date of the eclipse; the library sinks into the sand and returns to the Spirit World.
Narrow strip of land in the northeast of the Earth Kingdom, between the Eastern Lake and the sea: a dangerous route to Ba Sing Se.
Aang faces the sea serpent that guards the pass.
Forest on the west coast of the former colonies (later the United Republic).
Site of the final battle between Aang and Ozai during Sozin's Comet.
Center of the Harmony Restoration Movement crisis, right after the war.
Capital of the United Republic of Nations, a metropolis where people of every nation live.
Main setting of The Legend of Korra. After the battle against Kuvira, a spirit portal appears in the city center.
Metal city founded by Suyin Beifong, protected by petal-shaped domes.
Home of the Metal Clan; taken by Kuvira in Book 4.
Main haven of the series and home of the twins Pavi and Nisha.

Cosmopolitan metropolis of over a million people in the southeast of the Great Continent, laid out as an octagonal mandala. A system of narrow canyons protects it from the sandstorms and tornadoes of the Harshlands.
A haven built on the water, near the coast.
Northeast of Ellora, where Chameleon Bay used to be. The exact position of the islands in the bay is an estimate. Explored in Book 2.
A haven of the Great Continent known for its technical skill: it survives with technologies from before the Cataclysm.
Neighbor of the Lost Haven. Its position on the map is an estimate: the series has not shown where it is yet.
The "Lost Haven", which cut off contact with the rest of the world.
Probably in the former territory of the United Republic; official images from the series show Republic City overgrown with vegetation. Its position on the map is an estimate.
Mountainous southern islands, traditional territory of the Air Nomads, home to the Patola Mountain Range and Whaletail Island.
A great mountain chain in the north of the Great Continent, from south of Ba Sing Se to the Northern Air Temple.
Mountain range in the southwest of the Earth Kingdom, home to Omashu and the Cave of Two Lovers; considered the birthplace of earthbending.

The Hundred Year War is coming to an end. The Fire Nation rules colonies in the west of the Earth Kingdom, and the Air Nomads were wiped out a century ago. Aang, the last airbender, awakens from an iceberg and must master the four elements before Sozin's Comet.
Avatar: The Last Airbender (2005–2008) and the sequel comics.
Seventy years after the war, the former colonies form the United Republic of Nations, with modern Republic City. Korra reopens the spirit portals, faces the Red Lotus and stops Kuvira's Earth Empire.
The Legend of Korra (2012–2014) and the sequel comics.

About 225 years after Korra, a Cataclysm brought down the Four Nations. Humanity survives in seven isolated havens, surrounded by the Harshlands and battered by storms. The twins Pavi and Nisha, from Ellora, are at the center of the dispute over who is the true Avatar.
Avatar: Seven Havens (2026–). Series currently airing: information and positions may still change.
Feather Mountain — ruled by Empress Yeshe, it preserves the traditions of the Air Nomads; location not revealed
A haven of the Great Continent known for its technical skill: it survives with technologies from before the Cataclysm, such as motor vehicles.

The series only says it is on the Great Continent. The position is an estimate: Akasha should be the blue haven (the color of Ikaika's clothes), which the opening shows on the west coast of the continent. The fan theory that it is the former Zaofu does not match the official art, because Zaofu was inland in the southwest.
The "Lost Haven", which isolated itself from the rest of the world long before 399 AG. The Faceless believe there are no storms there and that benders and non-benders live in peace.
The violet haven, in the northwest of the Great Continent, roughly where Republic City used to be. The city appears overgrown with vegetation in the series' official images.
A haven ruled by Empress Yeshe, which preserves the traditions of the Air Nomads: arrow tattoos, flying bison and voluntary service by benders.

The series has not said where it is yet. The position is an estimate: it should be the green haven (the color of Yeshe's clothes), which the opening shows in the southwest of the Great Continent. Fans bet it is where Omashu used to be.
The seventh haven, whose name has not been revealed yet. It is in the former Fire Islands and is the most isolated of all.
The indigo haven. The series has only shown that it is in the Fire Islands. It is marked on the former Ember Island, which is the fans' bet, but the exact island has not been revealed.
